The `jq` optional chaining operator `[]?` was introduced in version 1.6. For better compatibility with older environments (e.g., Ubuntu 18.04 LTS) and to maintain consistency with the pattern used elsewhere in this file (see line 720), consider using the `(.labels // [])[]` idiom instead. Additionally, ensure that `stderr` is not suppressed (avoid `2>/dev/null`) so that syntax or system errors remain visible for debugging, as per repository guidelines.

```suggestion
printf '%s' "$issue_json" | jq -j --arg rs "$_RS" \
	'(.body // ""), $rs, ([(.labels // [])[].name] | join(",")), "\^@"'
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid suppressing stderr with 2>/dev/null on commands that parse configuration files (e.g., jq), as it can hide syntax errors and make debugging difficult.

+<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
+<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
+
+# Report Component Taxonomy
+
+Canonical contract for report agents, report templates, renderers, and SEO/GEO outputs. Keep this reference on-demand; do not duplicate it in always-loaded guidance.
+
+## Evidence Badge Model
+
+Every recommendation, claim, statistic, and tactic card should carry at least one evidence badge when the report makes an externally supportable claim.
+
+| Badge | Use for | Required evidence fields | Rendering notes |
+|-------|---------|--------------------------|-----------------|
+| `observed` | First-party crawl, audit, screenshot, log, analytics, search console, or manual review observations | `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `claim_supported`, `confidence`, `sensitivity` | Show as the strongest badge; pair with the inspected URL, artefact, or dataset label when safe. |
+| `sourced` | Third-party source, vendor documentation, public research, standards, or cited article | `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `claim_supported`, `confidence`, `sensitivity` | Link to the source card or citation list; avoid inline raw URLs in print-first layouts. |
+| `benchmark` | Competitive comparison, industry baseline, SERP/LLM mention comparison, or before/after metric | `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `claim_supported`, `confidence`, `sensitivity` | Render with comparison context: peer set, time window, and metric unit. |
+| `inferred` | Modelled conclusion from multiple signals where no single source proves the whole claim | `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `claim_supported`, `confidence`, `sensitivity` | Visually softer than direct evidence; include the inputs that support the inference. |
+| `estimate` | Forecast, projection, sizing, effort, cost, lift, or priority score | `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `claim_supported`, `confidence`, `sensitivity` | Label assumptions clearly; show ranges instead of false precision when possible. |
+
+### Shared evidence fields
+
+| Field | Required | Notes |
+|-------|----------|-------|
+| `source_id` | yes | Stable slug or report-local identifier, for example `gsc-2026-05` or `crawl-homepage`. |
+| `source_title` | yes | Human-readable source label safe for the report audience. |
+| `source_type` | yes | Use the config enum: `first_party`, `third_party`, `benchmark`, `model`, `manual_review`, `generated_artifact`. |
+| `observed_date` | yes | ISO date for when the evidence was observed or generated. |
+| `claim_supported` | yes | One sentence stating exactly what the evidence supports. |
+| `confidence` | yes | `high`, `medium`, or `low`; do not imply certainty from weak sources. |
+| `sensitivity` | yes | `public`, `internal`, `confidential`, or `redacted`; redact or aggregate before export when needed. |
+
+## Component Contract
+
+All components share these fields unless explicitly unnecessary: `id`, `component`, `title`, `body`, `evidence`, and `rendering_notes`. Components that create navigation also require `anchor`.
+
+| Component | Required fields | Rendering notes |
+|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|
+| Cover/meta | `id`, `component`, `title`, `subtitle`, `prepared_for`, `prepared_by`, `prepared_date`, `version`, `confidentiality`, `summary` | First page or report header. Keep sensitive client identifiers controlled by `confidentiality` and `sensitivity`. |
+| Sticky TOC | `id`, `component`, `title`, `items[]` with `label`, `anchor`, `level`, `status` | HTML renderers may pin it; Markdown/PDF renderers should degrade to a normal table of contents. |
+| Chapter hero heading | `id`, `component`, `title`, `anchor`, `kicker`, `summary`, `priority`, `evidence` | Start major sections with a short outcome-focused summary and optional priority badge. |
+| Action line | `id`, `component`, `action`, `owner`, `priority`, `effort`, `impact`, `due`, `evidence` | Use one sentence beginning with a verb. Render as a high-contrast strip or callout. |
+| Evidence badge | `id`, `component`, `badge`, `label`, `evidence` | Badge must map to the evidence badge enum. Prefer compact labels with a details link. |
+| What/Why/How tactic card | `id`, `component`, `title`, `what`, `why`, `how`, `priority`, `impact`, `effort`, `evidence` | Keep each section scannable. Use for recommendations that need rationale and execution steps. |
+| Code/example card | `id`, `component`, `title`, `language`, `code_or_example`, `context`, `copy_safe`, `evidence` | Mark whether content is illustrative or production-ready. Preserve fenced-code readability in Markdown. |
+| Good/bad rows | `id`, `component`, `title`, `rows[]` with `good`, `bad`, `reason`, `evidence` | Use for contrastive guidance. Avoid shaming language; focus on observable differences. |
+| Stats strip | `id`, `component`, `metrics[]` with `label`, `value`, `unit`, `delta`, `period`, `evidence` | Render as compact KPI cards. Always include period and unit. |
+| Facts table | `id`, `component`, `columns[]`, `rows[]`, `evidence` | Use for dense factual data. Keep columns stable across exports. |
+| Details note | `id`, `component`, `title`, `body`, `tone`, `evidence` | Render as aside/details block. Use for caveats, assumptions, or implementation notes. |
+| Industry card | `id`, `component`, `industry`, `title`, `context`, `pattern`, `implication`, `evidence` | Use when advice differs by vertical. Include the applicability boundary. |
+| Priority group | `id`, `component`, `title`, `priority`, `items[]`, `rationale`, `evidence` | Group actions by `critical`, `high`, `medium`, or `low`; sort critical first. |
+| Checklist | `id`, `component`, `title`, `items[]` with `label`, `status`, `owner`, `evidence` | Status values: `todo`, `doing`, `done`, `blocked`, `not_applicable`. |
+| Source card | `id`, `component`, `source_id`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `observed_date`, `summary`, `sensitivity` | Source cards back citations and should be collected in an appendix or source section. |
+| Myth callout | `id`, `component`, `myth`, `reality`, `why_it_matters`, `evidence` | Use sparingly to correct common misconceptions with evidence. |
+| Print rules | `id`, `component`, `page_size`, `margins`, `break_rules`, `hide_selectors`, `show_urls`, `footer` | Renderer-only component. Must not carry claims; use to preserve PDF-ready output. |
+
+## Rendering Rules
+
+- Renderers must preserve component order unless a template explicitly defines a safe reordering strategy.
+- Missing required fields should fail validation before export, not produce partial reports.
+- Evidence badges must link to a source card, footnote, appendix entry, or redacted evidence stub.
+- Sensitive fields must be redacted before public export; use `redacted` sensitivity rather than omitting evidence entirely.
+- Markdown renderers should remain readable without CSS; HTML renderers may add sticky navigation, cards, and badges; PDF renderers must respect print rules.
+
+## Verification
+
+```bash
+python3 -m json.tool .agents/configs/report-component-taxonomy.json.txt >/dev/null
+bunx markdownlint-cli2 ".agents/reference/report-component-taxonomy.md" ".agents/reference/domain-index.md"

+<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
+<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
+
+# Report Presentation Design
+
+<!-- AI-CONTEXT-START -->
+
+## Quick Reference
+
+- **Purpose**: Map report component taxonomy to DESIGN.md tokens and components
+  for Markdown, styled HTML, and PDF-ready reports.
+- **Use with**: `tools/design/design-md.md` for token format and
+  `tools/design/design-md-from-links.md` when deriving a report brand from URLs.
+- **Validation**: `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md`, contrast checks,
+  semantic HTML review, print preview, and PDF readability pass.
+- **Outputs**: DESIGN.md report tokens, HTML/CSS component guidance, and print
+  CSS considerations.
+
+<!-- AI-CONTEXT-END -->
+
+## Report Design Principles
+
+Reports are decision tools. Prioritise scannability, evidence traceability, and
+print-safe typography over decorative novelty.
+
+- Put the answer first: executive summary, status, priority, next action.
+- Make evidence legible: source cards, citations, confidence badges, timestamps,
+  and clear distinction between observed facts and recommendations.
+- Use one component language across Markdown, HTML, and PDF so exports do not
+  lose meaning.
+- Reserve strong colour for status, priority, and action; keep long-form reading
+  high-contrast and calm.
+- Design every component for narrow screens and paged media from the start.
+
+## DESIGN.md Token Foundation
+
+Add or verify these token groups in `DESIGN.md`:
+
+| Token group | Report role |
+|-------------|-------------|
+| `colors.background`, `colors.surface`, `colors.on-surface` | Page, cards, and default text |
+| `colors.primary`, `colors.secondary`, `colors.tertiary` | Brand accents, links, chapter markers |
+| `colors.success`, `colors.warning`, `colors.error`, `colors.info` | Evidence/status badges and priority states |
+| `colors.outline`, `colors.muted`, `colors.highlight` | Dividers, secondary text, pull quotes, search highlights |
+| `typography.headline-*` | Cover title, chapter heroes, section headings |
+| `typography.body-*`, `typography.label-*`, `typography.code` | Narrative, metadata, badges, examples |
+| `spacing.*` | Page rhythm, card padding, table density, print margins |
+| `rounded.*` | Cards, badges, code blocks, evidence pills |
+| `components.*` | Taxonomy components below |
+
+## Component Taxonomy Mapping
+
+Every report component should map to a named `components:` token entry so build
+agents can produce consistent Markdown, HTML, and PDF output.
+
+| Taxonomy component | DESIGN.md component token | Required design decisions |
+|--------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
+| Cover/meta | `report-cover`, `report-meta` | Title hierarchy, client/project metadata, date/version, confidentiality marker |
+| Executive summary | `report-summary` | Key finding density, status colour, 3-5 bullet rhythm |
+| Sticky/table of contents | `report-toc`, `report-toc-active` | Active state, anchor offsets, mobile collapse, print fallback |
+| Chapter hero | `report-chapter-hero` | Section label, title, lead paragraph, page-break handling |
+| Action line | `report-action-line` | Verb-first action, owner, due date, priority indicator |
+| Evidence badge | `report-evidence-badge-*` | Confidence/status colours, label typography, icon/text fallback |
+| What/Why/How tactic card | `report-tactic-card`, `report-tactic-step` | Three-part structure, priority, effort/impact chips |
+| Code/example card | `report-code-card`, `report-example-card` | Mono type, copy affordance, line wrapping, caption/source |
+| Good/bad row | `report-comparison-row-good`, `report-comparison-row-bad` | Paired contrast, accessible icons, avoid colour-only meaning |
+| Stats strip | `report-stats-strip`, `report-stat` | Large numerals, labels, trend deltas, mobile wrapping |
+| Facts table | `report-facts-table` | Caption, headers, zebra/row hover, numeric alignment, source column |
+| Details note | `report-details-note` | Collapsible HTML behaviour, Markdown fallback, print-expanded default |
+| Industry card | `report-industry-card` | Segment label, benchmark, opportunity, caveat |
+| Priority group | `report-priority-group-*` | Critical/high/medium/low palette, sorting, section intro |
+| Checklist | `report-checklist`, `report-checklist-item` | Done/open/blocked states, tap target size, print checkboxes |
+| Source card | `report-source-card` | URL/title, author/publisher, access date, evidence quote |
+| Myth callout | `report-myth-callout` | Myth/fact contrast, warning tone without alarmism |
+| Recommendation | `report-recommendation` | Decision, rationale, expected outcome, next owner |
+| Risk/assumption note | `report-risk-note`, `report-assumption-note` | Severity, uncertainty, validation path |
+| Timeline/roadmap | `report-timeline`, `report-milestone` | Sequence, dependencies, date labels, page-break-safe rows |
+| Appendix | `report-appendix`, `report-footnote` | Smaller but readable type, source density, cross-references |
+
+## Evidence Badge Taxonomy
+
+Use badges to make source strength explicit without overwhelming the reader.
+
+| Badge | Meaning | Typical colour role |
+|-------|---------|---------------------|
+| `observed` | Directly measured in source, tool output, or screenshot | `info` |
+| `verified` | Reproduced by this session or automated check | `success` |
+| `inferred` | Reasoned from partial evidence; needs confirmation | `warning` |
+| `unsupported` | Claim lacks usable evidence; treat as backlog or remove | `error` |
+| `benchmark` | Compared against a known baseline or competitor | `secondary` |
+| `recommendation` | Advisory action derived from evidence | `primary` |
+
+Pair every badge with text, not just colour. In print, preserve the label and add
+border/shape differences so grayscale output remains meaningful.
+
+## HTML and CSS Guidance
+
+- Use semantic HTML: `<main>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, `<nav>`, `<table>`,
+  `<caption>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<details>`, `<summary>`, `<figure>`, and
+  `<figcaption>` where appropriate.
+- Expose source links as real anchors with visible URL or citation labels in PDF.
+- Use CSS custom properties generated from DESIGN.md tokens; avoid hard-coded
+  one-off report colours.
+- Keep sticky TOC and interactive details progressive: the report remains readable
+  when printed, saved to PDF, or viewed without JavaScript.
+- Charts need text alternatives: title, summary, data table fallback, and clear
+  colour/shape encoding.
+- Code blocks should wrap or scroll in HTML, but print with readable line breaks
+  and captions.
+
+## PDF and Print Styling
+
+Add print rules alongside screen CSS:
+
+```css
+@media print {
+  @page { margin: 18mm 16mm; }
+  body { color: var(--color-on-surface); background: #fff; font-size: 11pt; }
body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The CSS variable `--color-on-surface` uses a singular prefix, but the DESIGN.md token group is `colors`. To ensure compatibility with standard exporters (which typically use the group name as a prefix), this should likely be `--colors-on-surface`. Additionally, hardcoding `background: #fff` ignores the `colors.background` token; using the token with a white fallback is more consistent with the design system.

```suggestion
  body { color: var(--colors-on-surface); background: var(--colors-background, #fff); font-size: 11pt; }
```

+
+Use badges to make source strength explicit without overwhelming the reader.

+| Badge | Meaning | Typical colour role |
+|-------|---------|---------------------|

The `render_mermaid_svg` function is extremely limited and contains several logic issues that may produce misleading diagrams:
- **Node Deduplication Bug**: It deduplicates nodes by their label instead of their ID (lines 199-200). This means multiple distinct nodes with the same label will be merged into a single box.
- **Linear Flow Assumption**: The arrow rendering logic (lines 229-240) assumes a simple linear sequence (node `i` to node `i+1`) and completely ignores the actual connections defined in the Mermaid source.
- **Hardcoded Pathing**: The `H 104` value in the path calculation (line 234) is hardcoded for the first column's center and will result in broken paths for multi-column layouts.
- **Arrowhead Gaps**: Arrowheads are rendered with significant gaps from the target nodes due to the margin calculations.

Consider documenting these limitations or implementing a more robust ID-based mapping for nodes and edges.

In Markdown, backslashes are generally used to escape the following character, and a double backslash `\\` should always be unescaped to a single literal backslash `\`. To ensure consistency and avoid data corruption in table cells, the unescaping logic should be applied to all characters, not just pipes.

Using `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'` to extract the issue number from `session_key` is fragile because it assumes the session key always ends with the issue number. If the session key contains any suffix (e.g., attempt number, timestamp, or run ID), this regex will either extract the wrong number or fail entirely. 

Since we already verify that `session_key` starts with `issue-`, we can use pure Bash parameter expansion to robustly extract the issue number. This is also significantly more efficient as it avoids spawning external processes (`printf` and `grep`).

```suggestion
	local temp="${session_key#issue-}"
	local issue_number="${temp%%[!0-9]*}"
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Spawning `printf` and `grep` inside a `while read` loop for each branch PR is inefficient. Since we are in Bash, we can use a pure Bash pattern match with newline padding to perform the exact line match in-process. This is extremely fast and avoids spawning any subprocesses.

```suggestion
	local branch_pr_number=""
	local padded_issue_prs=$'\n'"$issue_pr_numbers"$'\n'
	while IFS= read -r branch_pr_number; do
		[[ -n "$branch_pr_number" ]] || continue
		if [[ "$padded_issue_prs" == *$'\n'"$branch_pr_number"$'\n'* ]]; then
			print_info "[lifecycle] worker_external_terminal complete session=${session_key} issue=${issue_number} branch=${branch_name} pr=${branch_pr_number}"
			return 0
		fi
	done <<<
"$branch_pr_numbers"
```

To make git operations in scripts more robust, dynamically and explicitly determine the default branch instead of relying on the current checkout. Implement a fallback mechanism to find the branch, for example: try `origin/HEAD`, then common names like `main`/`master`, and finally `HEAD`. Additionally, when declaring and assigning local variables in shell scripts, separate the `local` declaration from the assignment if command substitution is involved, to ensure exit code safety.

```suggestion
	local branch_name
	branch_name=$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null || git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
```

The new parameter expansion logic `local temp="${session_key#issue-}"` followed by `local issue_number="${temp%%[!0-9]*}"` changes the behavior compared to the original `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'` regex.

Specifically, if `session_key` contains non-digit characters between `issue-` and the trailing digits (e.g., `issue-gateway-123`), the original code correctly extracted `123`, whereas the new code will yield an empty string because `temp` starts with a non-digit character (`g`).

To optimize this in pure Bash while preserving the exact original behavior, you can use Bash's built-in regular expression matching operator `=~`.

```suggestion
	local issue_number=""
	[[ "$session_key" =~ ([0-9]+)$ ]] && issue_number="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
```

```python
def _connect(path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection | None:
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        return conn
    except sqlite3.Error as err:
        print(f"Warning: Could not connect to database at {path}: {err}", file=sys.stderr)
        return None
```

Using `init=False` on a dataclass prevents the generation of the `__init__` method. Consequently, default values and default factories (such as `field(default_factory=list)` for `source_session_ids`) are never initialized on the instance. If a `SessionReport` is instantiated without explicitly setting `source_session_ids`, accessing it will return the `dataclasses.Field` descriptor object instead of a list, which can lead to unexpected runtime errors.

It is highly recommended to keep the default `init=True` behavior to ensure proper initialization and type safety.


![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `any` is more idiomatic, concise, and efficient in `jq` than mapping the array and checking the index. It directly checks if any element in the labels array matches the criteria without creating intermediate arrays.

```suggestion
	printf '%s\n' "$issue_json" | jq -e '
		((.title // "") | startswith("[Supervisor:"))
		or any((.labels // [])[]; (.name // .) == "supervisor")
	' >/dev/null 2>&1
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In `jq`, use the fallback operator `//` to provide a default value for expressions that might result in `null`, such as `min_by` or `max_by` on empty or invalid inputs.
</details>

+#          2=API/parse error

+	local repo_slug="$1"

body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In GitHub CLI, `gh pr checks` exits with non-zero codes when checks are failing or pending (specifically, `1` for failed checks and `2` for pending checks).

Using `|| return 2` directly on the command assignment means that whenever there are pending or failed checks, the function will prematurely return `2` (API/parse error) instead of parsing the JSON and returning `1` (not passing). This masks the actual check status and incorrectly logs a fallback failure.

We should capture the exit code and only return `2` if the exit code is not `0`, `1`, or `2`.

```suggestion
	local checks_json
	local gh_exit
	gh_exit=0
	checks_json=$(gh pr checks "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --required --json name,state,bucket 2>/dev/null) || gh_exit=$?
	if [[ $gh_exit -ne 0 && $gh_exit -ne 1 && $gh_exit -ne 2 ]]; then
		return 2
	fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When declaring and assigning local variables in shell scripts, separate the `local` declaration from the assignment if command substitution is involved, to ensure exit code safety. For consistency, this pattern should be maintained even for simple assignments.
2. In shell scripts, capture a command's exit code in a variable instead of using `$?` directly in conditionals. This aligns with ShellCheck SC2181 and improves clarity for multi-way branches.
</details>

	fi

Using `\n` in the replacement string of `sed` is a GNU extension and is not portable to BSD `sed` (the default on macOS). On macOS, it will literally insert the character `n` or `\n` instead of a newline, resulting in a malformed `credentials.sh` file. To insert a newline portably, use a backslash followed by a literal newline. Additionally, using POSIX character classes like `[[:space:]]` instead of non-standard shortcuts like `\s` ensures better portability across regex engines.

```suggestion
		sed -i.bak -E "s/^([[:space:]]*)((export[[:space:]]+)?(\${deprecated_vars})=.*)$/\\1\${deprecation_note}\\
```

If `_run_cleanups` fails to execute any commands (for example, due to a bug in the reversal logic), the `$order_file` will never be created. Consequently, the command `actual_order="$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$order_file")"` on line 52 will fail with a `No such file or directory` error, causing the test script to crash immediately due to `set -e` instead of failing gracefully and reporting the assertion failure. Initializing the file with `touch` ensures the test fails gracefully with a clear assertion message.

```suggestion
order_file="$TMPDIR_TEST/order.txt"
stderr_file="$TMPDIR_TEST/stderr.txt"
touch "$order_file"
```

This means the regexes will fail to match on modern Bash versions, causing benign failures to be misclassified as warnings. When a merge is already in progress, returning immediately without calling `_handle_post_merge_actions` will cause the PR's post-merge lifecycle to be skipped entirely. This means the closing comment won't be posted, the linked ticket won't be closed or unlocked, the solved labels won't be set, and sequential phase auto-filing (`auto_file_next_phase`) won't be triggered.

To prevent these orphaned states, invoke `_handle_post_merge_actions` before returning. Additionally, propagate the exit code of `_handle_post_merge_actions` using `return $?` instead of masking potential errors with a hardcoded `return 0`.

```suggestion

		echo "[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic merge: PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} already has a merge in progress; counting as merge progress (GH#24383): ${merge_output}" >>"$LOGFILE"

```

There are three issues with the current `creationPatterns` regexes:
1. **Greedy matching across command boundaries**: The use of `[\s\S]*` and `[\s\S]+` allows matching across command boundaries (such as `;`, `&&`, `||`, and newlines). This can lead to false positives where an unrelated command earlier in a chained shell command matches, bypassing the signature check.
2. **`tee` command redirection**: `tee` is grouped with `echo`, `printf`, and `cat` in a pattern requiring `>` or `>>`. However, `tee` writes to files passed as direct arguments (e.g., `tee file.md`) rather than using shell redirection.
3. **`touch` options**: The `touch` pattern does not allow for optional flags (e.g., `touch -m file.md`).

### Efficiency & Performance Optimization

The current implementation makes two separate `gh pr view` calls per closer PR inside the loop to fetch the `state` and `mergedAt` fields. Since `gh` CLI invocations involve network requests and process spawning, this is highly inefficient and can significantly slow down the execution.

We can optimize this by:
1. Combining both fields into a single `gh pr view` call and parsing them together.
2. Checking if `closer_numbers` is empty upfront to avoid entering the loop entirely.
3. Using a here-string (`<<<`) instead of a multi-line heredoc for cleaner syntax.

Additionally, to ensure robustness and ease of debugging, do not suppress stderr with `2>/dev/null` so that actual syntax or system errors remain visible, and use `|| true` to prevent the script from exiting when `jq` fails on an optional lookup.

```suggestion
	closer_numbers=$(printf '%s' "$issue_json" | jq -r '.closedByPullRequestsReferences[]?.number // empty' || true)
	[[ -n "$closer_numbers" ]] || return 1

	while IFS= read -r closer_number; do
		[[ "$closer_number" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
		[[ "$closer_number" != "$current_pr" ]] || continue
		local pr_info
		pr_info=$(gh pr view "$closer_number" --repo "$repo_slug" \
			--json state,mergedAt --jq '"\(.state // "") \(.mergedAt // "")"') || continue
		local pr_state="" merged_at=""
		read -r pr_state merged_at <<< "$pr_info"
		if [[ "$pr_state" == "MERGED" || -n "$merged_at" ]]; then
			printf '%s' "$closer_number"
			return 0
		fi
	done <<< "$closer_numbers"
	return 1
```

The `canonical_title` definition checks if the title starts with the task ID followed by a colon or a space. However, if a task is named exactly `t1000` (without any trailing colon or space), it will not be recognized as canonical. If there is also an incidental match (e.g., a review follow-up), the helper will fall back to the incidental match instead of preferring the exact match.

To make this more robust, we should also check if the title is exactly equal to the needle.

```suggestion
		def canonical_title:
			(.title // "" | ascii_downcase) as $title
			| ("t" + ($task_id | ascii_downcase)) as $needle
			| ($title == $needle or ($title | startswith($needle + ":")) or ($title | startswith($needle + " ")));
```

Since the App Store Connect API only defines two states for `profileState` (`ACTIVE` and `INVALID`), filtering by `--profile-state ACTIVE,INVALID` is redundant as it returns all profiles (equivalent to omitting the filter entirely).

```suggestion
asc profiles list --profile-state ACTIVE --paginate --output json
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If a session title or parent title contains newline characters (which is common for titles generated from multi-line commit messages or PR descriptions), the row-parsing loop in Bash (`read -r`) will split the row across multiple lines. This corrupts the parsed fields and results in incomplete or broken JSON/table output.

To prevent this, we can sanitize newlines and carriage returns directly in the SQL query using SQLite's `REPLACE` function, ensuring each row is strictly a single line.

```suggestion
	"$SQLITE3_BIN" -readonly -separator $'\037' "$db" "
SELECT '$source', $status_expr, s.id, REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE($title_expr, ''), char(10), ' '), char(13), ''), COALESCE($directory_expr, ''),
       COALESCE($project_expr, ''), COALESCE($parent_expr, ''), REPLACE(REPLACE($parent_title_expr, char(10), ' '), char(13), ''),
       COALESCE($created_expr, ''), COALESCE($updated_expr, ''), $mismatch_expr
FROM $from_join
WHERE $where
ORDER BY COALESCE($updated_expr, $created_expr, 0) DESC, s.id
LIMIT $limit;" 2>/dev/null || return 1
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The table-valued function `pragma_table_info('session')` was introduced in SQLite 3.16.0. While modern systems typically have newer versions, using the standard `PRAGMA table_info(session)` is universally compatible across all SQLite 3 versions and does not rely on table-valued function support.

```suggestion
_sessions_column_exists() {
	local db="$1"
	local column="$2"
	if "$SQLITE3_BIN" -readonly "$db" "PRAGMA table_info('session');" 2>/dev/null | cut -d'|' -f2 | grep -q "^$column$"; then
		return 0
	fi
	return 1
}
```

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn
+# pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh — Dispatch bounded PR-loop workers for unresolved active-PR review threads.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh scan <repo_slug> [repo_path]
+#   pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch <repo_slug> <repo_path>
+#   pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dry-run <repo_slug> [repo_path]
+#
+# This helper is intentionally conservative: it never resolves review threads
+# itself. It only detects unresolved, non-outdated bot review threads on open
+# non-draft PRs and dispatches a bounded worker prompt to verify and respond via
+# the existing PR-review loop model. The worker must read/verify the thread
+# before editing code or resolving/commenting.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")" && pwd)"
+# shellcheck source=shared-constants.sh
+[[ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh" ]] && source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh"
+
+LOGFILE="${LOGFILE:-${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log}"
+STATE_DIR="${AIDEVOPS_PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_STATE_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/pr-review-thread-response}"
+HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER="${HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/headless-runtime-helper.sh}"
+
+PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_PR_LIMIT="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_PR_LIMIT:-50}"
+PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_MAX_PER_REPO="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_MAX_PER_REPO:-2}"
+PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_COOLDOWN="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_COOLDOWN:-3600}"
+PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_MODEL="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_MODEL:-}"
+PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_BOT_RE="${PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_BOT_RE:-coderabbitai|gemini-code-assist|claude-review|gpt-review|augment-code|augmentcode|copilot}"
+PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE="true"
+PRRTS_BOOL_FALSE="false"

+_prrts_ensure_dirs() {
+	local log_dir=""
+	log_dir="$(dirname "$LOGFILE")"
+	mkdir -p "$log_dir" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_log() {
+	local message="$1"
+	_prrts_ensure_dirs
+	printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" "$message" >>"$LOGFILE"
+	return 0
+}

+_prrts_usage() {
+	printf 'Usage: %s {scan|dispatch|dry-run} <repo_slug> [repo_path]\n' "$(basename "$0")"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_safe_slug() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	printf '%s' "$repo_slug" | tr '/:' '--'
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_parse_repo_slug() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local owner_var="$2"
+	local name_var="$3"
+	local owner="${repo_slug%%/*}"
+	local name="${repo_slug##*/}"
+	printf -v "$owner_var" '%s' "$owner"
+	printf -v "$name_var" '%s' "$name"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_normalise_int() {
+	local value="$1"
+	local default_value="$2"
+	local min_value="$3"
+	[[ "$value" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || value="$default_value"
+	if [[ "$value" -lt "$min_value" ]]; then
+		value="$min_value"
+	fi
+	printf '%s\n' "$value"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_list_open_prs() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local limit=""
+	limit="$(_prrts_normalise_int "$PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_PR_LIMIT" "50" "1")"
+	gh pr list --repo "$repo_slug" --state open --limit "$limit" \
+		--json number,title,isDraft,labels,headRefName,author \
+		--jq '.[] | [.number, (.title // "" | gsub("[\t\r\n]"; " ")), (.isDraft | tostring), ([.labels[].name] | join(",")), (.headRefName // ""), (.author.login // "")] | @tsv'
+	return $?
+}
+
+_prrts_fetch_review_threads_json() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local owner="" name="" response="" rc=0
+	_prrts_parse_repo_slug "$repo_slug" owner name
+	# shellcheck disable=SC2016
+	response=$(gh api graphql \
+		-F owner="$owner" -F name="$name" -F pr="$pr_number" \
+		-f query='

+				repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
+					pullRequest(number: $pr) {
+						reviewThreads(first: 100) {
+							nodes {
+								id
+								isResolved
+								isOutdated
+								comments(first: 1) {
+									nodes {
+										author { login }
+										path
+										line
+										url
+										updatedAt
+									}
+								}
+							}
+						}
+					}
+				}
+			}
+		' 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?

+	fi

+		_prrts_log "fetch: malformed reviewThreads response for ${repo_slug}#${pr_number}"
+		return 2
+	fi

+
+_prrts_review_thread_summary() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local json="" summary="" rc=0

+	if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+		return "$rc"
+	fi
+	summary=$(printf '%s' "$json" | jq -r --arg bots "$PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_BOT_RE" '
+		[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]?
+			| select((.isResolved // false) == false)
+			| select((.isOutdated // false) == false)
+			| {thread_id: (.id // ""), comment: (.comments.nodes[0]? // {})}
+			| select((.comment.author.login // "") | test($bots; "i"))
+		] as $threads
+		| [
+			($threads | length),
+			($threads | map((.thread_id // "") + ":" + (.comment.url // "")) | sort | join(",")),
+			($threads | map("\(.comment.author.login // "bot") on \(.comment.path // "<no path>"):\(.comment.line // "?")") | unique | .[:5] | join("; "))
+		] | @tsv
+	' 2>/dev/null) || {
+		_prrts_log "summary: jq failed for ${repo_slug}#${pr_number}"
+		return 2
+	}
+	printf '%s\n' "$summary"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_labels_block_response() {
+	local labels_csv="$1"
+	local labels=",${labels_csv},"
+	case "$labels" in
+	*,hold-for-review,* | *,needs-maintainer-review,*)
+		return 0
+		;;
+	*)
+		return 1
+		;;
+	esac
+}
+
+cmd_scan() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_rows="" summary="" rc=0
+	local pr_number="" title="" is_draft="" labels="" head_ref="" author=""
+	local thread_count="" fingerprint="" preview=""
+
+	pr_rows="$(_prrts_list_open_prs "$repo_slug")" || {
+		_prrts_log "scan: failed to list open PRs for ${repo_slug}"
+		return 0
+	}
+
+	while IFS=$'\t' read -r pr_number title is_draft labels head_ref author; do
+		[[ -n "$pr_number" ]] || continue
+		if [[ "$is_draft" == "$PRRTS_BOOL_TRUE" ]]; then
+			_prrts_log "scan: ${repo_slug}#${pr_number} skipped — draft PR"
+			continue
+		fi
+		if _prrts_labels_block_response "$labels"; then
+			_prrts_log "scan: ${repo_slug}#${pr_number} skipped — protected label present (${labels})"
+			continue
+		fi
+		rc=0
+		summary="$(_prrts_review_thread_summary "$repo_slug" "$pr_number")" || rc=$?
+		if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+			_prrts_log "scan: ${repo_slug}#${pr_number} skipped — review-thread fetch failed"
+			continue
+		fi
+		IFS=$'\t' read -r thread_count fingerprint preview <<<"$summary"
+		[[ "$thread_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || thread_count=0
+		if [[ "$thread_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
+			printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
+				"$pr_number" "$thread_count" "$fingerprint" "$title" "$head_ref" "$author" "$preview"
+		fi
+	done <<<"$pr_rows"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_state_file() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local safe_slug=""
+	safe_slug="$(_prrts_safe_slug "$repo_slug")"
+	printf '%s/%s-%s.state\n' "$STATE_DIR" "$safe_slug" "$pr_number"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_session_key() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local safe_slug=""
+	safe_slug="$(_prrts_safe_slug "$repo_slug")"
+	printf 'pr-review-thread-response-%s-%s\n' "$safe_slug" "$pr_number"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_worker_active() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local session_key="" process_command=""
+	session_key="$(_prrts_session_key "$repo_slug" "$pr_number")"
+	while IFS= read -r process_command; do
+		case "$process_command" in
+		*"$session_key"*) return 0 ;;
+		esac
+	done < <(ps axwwo command 2>/dev/null || true)
+	return 1
+}
+
+_prrts_read_state() {
+	local state_file="$1"
+	local fingerprint_var="$2"
+	local dispatched_var="$3"
+	local key="" value=""
+	local state_fingerprint="" state_dispatched_at="0"
+	if [[ -f "$state_file" ]]; then
+		while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
+			case "$key" in
+			fingerprint) state_fingerprint="$value" ;;
+			dispatched_at) state_dispatched_at="$value" ;;
+			esac
+		done <"$state_file"
+	fi
+	[[ "$state_dispatched_at" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || state_dispatched_at=0

+	printf -v "$dispatched_var" '%s' "$state_dispatched_at"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_prrts_should_dispatch() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local fingerprint="$3"
+	local now_epoch="$4"
+	local state_file="" last_fingerprint="" dispatched_at="0" cooldown="" age_seconds="0"
+	state_file="$(_prrts_state_file "$repo_slug" "$pr_number")"
+	cooldown="$(_prrts_normalise_int "$PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_COOLDOWN" "3600" "60")"
+	_prrts_read_state "$state_file" last_fingerprint dispatched_at
+
+	if _prrts_worker_active "$repo_slug" "$pr_number"; then
+		_prrts_log "dispatch: ${repo_slug}#${pr_number} skipped — response worker already active"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	age_seconds=$((now_epoch - dispatched_at))

body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If a pull request author has been deleted, the `author` object returned by the GitHub API can be `null`. Attempting to access `.author.login` directly will cause `jq` to fail with a `Cannot index null with string "login"` error, which will halt the PR listing and skip the entire scan for this repository.

Using optional chaining (`.author?.login`) prevents this crash and safely falls back to the default empty string.

```suggestion
		--jq '.[] | [.number, (.title // "" | gsub("[\\t\\r\\n]"; " ")), (.isDraft | tostring), ([.labels[].name] | join(",")), (.headRefName // ""), (.author?.login // "")] | @tsv'
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In `jq`, use the fallback operator `//` to provide a default value for expressions that might result in `null`.
</details>

+								isResolved

+	local pr_number="$2"

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Similar to the check on line 150, if the comment author is deleted/null, string interpolation of `\(.comment.author.login)` will fail.

Using optional chaining (`\(.comment.author?.login // "bot")`) prevents `jq` from crashing.

```suggestion
($threads | map("\\(.comment.author?.login // \"bot\") on \\(.comment.path // \"<no path>\"):\\(.comment.line // \"?\\")") | unique | .[:5] | join(\"; \"))
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In `jq`, use the fallback operator `//` to provide a default value for expressions that might result in `null`.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `shared_db` is a shared database that can be locked by concurrent workers or interactive sessions. Querying it without a busy timeout (e.g., `-cmd ".timeout 5000"`) can lead to silent failures when copying the schema, resulting in missing tables in the isolated `worker_db` and subsequent migration sync failures. Adding a busy timeout to both `sqlite3` commands ensures robustness under concurrent execution.

```suggestion
	if [[ -z "$has_schema_migrations" ]]; then
		sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 5000" "$shared_db" ".schema __drizzle_migrations" 2>/dev/null | sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 5000" "$worker_db" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
	fi
	if [[ -z "$has_data_migration" ]]; then
		sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 5000" "$shared_db" ".schema data_migration" 2>/dev/null | sqlite3 -cmd ".timeout 5000" "$worker_db" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
	fi
```

There are three problems in this block that prevent the trusted Dependabot gate from working for standard single (non-grouped) Dependabot updates:

1. **CRLF Line Endings**: GitHub PR bodies often contain carriage returns (`\r`). If not stripped, the extracted dependency names will contain trailing `\r` characters, causing allowlist matching to fail.
2. **Missing Package Manager for Single Updates**: For non-grouped updates, there is no group name in the PR body, so `package_manager` is empty. This prevents matching prefix-qualified entries like `pip:pyarrow` in the allowlist. We can robustly infer the package manager by inspecting the files changed in the PR.
3. **Missing Dependency Name for Single Updates**: Single (non-grouped) Dependabot updates do not contain the `- dependency-name:` YAML block in their body. We should fall back to extracting the dependency name from the first line of the body or the PR title.

```shell
	local body package_manager dependencies dependency_name allowed_count=0
	body=$(printf '%s' "$pr_json" | jq -r '.body // ""' | tr -d '\r') || body=""
	package_manager=$(printf '%s' "$body" | sed -nE 's/^Bumps the ([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+) group.*$/\1/p' | head -1)
	if [[ -z "$package_manager" ]]; then
		local files
		files=$(printf '%s' "$pr_json" | jq -r '.files[]?.path') || files=""
		if echo "$files" | grep -qE 'package(-lock)?\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock'; then
			package_manager="npm"
		elif echo "$files" | grep -qE 'requirements.*\.txt|pyproject\.toml|poetry\.lock|uv\.lock|Pipfile\.lock'; then
			package_manager="pip"
		elif echo "$files" | grep -qE 'Cargo\.(toml|lock)'; then
			package_manager="cargo"
		elif echo "$files" | grep -qE 'go\.(mod|sum)'; then
			package_manager="gomod"
```

If the `trusted-dependabot-updates.conf` file is edited on Windows or contains carriage returns (`\r`), the parsed entries will contain trailing `\r` characters, causing exact matching with `grep -Fxq` to fail. Strip `\r` characters from the parsed entries to ensure robust matching across different platforms.

```suggestion
	local entries
	entries=$(sed -E 's/[[:space:]]*#.*$//; s/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//' "$conf_path" | tr -d '\r' | sed '/^$/d') || entries=""
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `gh api graphql` call is executed directly without capturing its exit status. Since `set -euo pipefail` is active, any API failure (e.g., network issues, invalid permissions, or rate limits) will cause the entire script to terminate abruptly. Capturing the exit status and logging the failure gracefully prevents unexpected crashes and provides better observability. Avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` to ensure that authentication or system issues remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
	local rc=0
	gh api graphql \
		-F thread="$thread_id" -F body="$body" \
		-f query='
			mutation($thread: ID!, $body: String!) {
				addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input: {pullRequestReviewThreadId: $thread, body: $body}) {
					comment { id url }
				}
			}
		' >/dev/null || rc=$?
	if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
		_prrts_log "reply: failed to post in-thread response for ${repo_slug} thread ${thread_id} (rc=${rc})"
		return 1
	fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid using '2>/dev/null' for blanket suppression of command errors in shell scripts to ensure that authentication, syntax, or system issues remain visible for debugging.
2. In shell scripts, capture a command's exit code in a variable instead of using `$?` directly in conditionals. This aligns with ShellCheck SC2181 and improves clarity for multi-way branches.
</details>

The function `_nmr_current_actor_can_post_maintainer_approval` is called in a loop for every open issue. Inside this function, `gh api user` and `gh api repos/${slug}/collaborators/${actor}/permission` are called repeatedly. To improve efficiency and avoid redundant I/O, refactor the function to optionally accept pre-computed values as arguments. The function can then skip the API calls if the values are provided, while retaining the ability to compute them itself as a fallback. Also, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` so that authentication or API errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
_nmr_current_actor_can_post_maintainer_approval() {
	local slug="$1"
	local actor="${2:-}"
	local actor_permission="${3:-}"

	if [[ -z "$actor" ]]; then
		actor=$(gh api user --jq '.login // empty') || return 1
	fi
	[[ -n "$actor" ]] || return 1

	if [[ -z "$actor_permission" ]]; then
		actor_permission=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/collaborators/${actor}/permission" --jq '.permission // "none"') || actor_permission="none"
	fi

	case "$actor_permission" in
	admin | maintain | write) return 0 ;;
	*) return 1 ;;
	esac
}
```

To prevent `jq` from returning the literal string `"null"` when the `.permission` key is missing or its value is null, use the fallback operator `// ""` in the `--jq` filter. This ensures that the resulting variable is an empty string, making non-empty checks (e.g., `[[ -n "$var" ]]`) sufficient and robust.

```suggestion
github_app_api_call read rest-core gh api \
  "/repos/${repo_slug}/collaborators/${author}/permission" --jq '.permission // ""'

# Where shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh is already sourced, prefer:
_rest_api_call read gh api \
  "/repos/${repo_slug}/collaborators/${author}/permission" --jq '.permission // ""'
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When parsing a JSON value in a shell script using `jq -r '.key // ""'`, the resulting variable will be an empty string if the key is missing or its value is `null`. Therefore, a check for the literal string "null" is redundant, and a non-empty check (e.g., `[[ -n "$var" ]]`) is sufficient.
</details>

+
+By default, downstream callers delegate to `marcusquinn/aidevops`. Organizations that mirror or review reusable workflows in an organization-owned repository can configure the expected target in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`:

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `jq` invocation passes several static strings as arguments (`--arg result_field "result"`, etc.) and uses dynamic indexing `.[$result_field]`. Since these values are constant, we can simplify the filter by referencing `.result` directly and hardcoding the status strings. Additionally, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on `jq` to prevent hiding potential syntax or parsing errors, making debugging easier.

```suggestion

		--argjson window "$window_seconds" '
		def result_match:
			(.result // "") as $r
			| if $mode == "local" then $r == "local_error"
			  else ($r == "success" or $r == "blocked")
			  end;
		[.[] | select((.session_key // "") == $key)
			| select(((.ts // 0) | tonumber) >= (now - $window))
			| select(result_match)] | length
	' "$metrics_file" || printf '%s' '0')
```

### Ambiguity and Potential Corruption with Backreference Followed by Digits

Using `\1$main_agents` in the replacement string expands to `\1<number>` (e.g., `\112` if `$main_agents` is 12, or `\15` if `$main_agents` is 5).

In many `sed` implementations, regex engines, or compatible tools (such as `perl` or certain shells/clones), a backslash followed by multiple digits is interpreted as an octal escape sequence or a multi-digit backreference:
- `\112` is parsed as octal for the character `J`.
- `\15` is parsed as octal for a carriage return (`\r`).

This can lead to corrupted text in the README (e.g., `J primary agents` or a carriage return instead of the actual count).

#### Solution
To avoid any ambiguity and prevent backreferences from being immediately followed by digits, split the replacement into two separate, clean `sed` commands—one for the tilde-prefixed counts and one for the non-tilde counts.

```suggestion
	sed_inplace -E "s/~[0-9][0-9,]* (main|domain|primary) agents/~$main_agents \1 agents/g" "$readme_file"
	sed_inplace -E "s/([0-9][0-9,]*) (main|domain|primary) agents/$main_agents \2 agents/g" "$readme_file"
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

### Finding: Potential False Negatives due to Substring Matching without Word Boundaries

In the regular expression defined for `NOOP_RE`, several keywords and phrases are matched as substrings without word boundaries (`\b`). This can lead to unexpected false negatives where genuine, actionable review summaries are incorrectly filtered out.

#### Specific Vulnerabilities:
1. **`no suggestions to (add|provide|make)`**:
   - The word `add` is a prefix of `address`.
   - If a bot writes: *"I have no suggestions to address this specific warning."*, this is an actionable statement indicating a warning exists but no automated fix is suggested.
   - However, because `add` matches the prefix of `address`, the entire review summary will be incorrectly suppressed.
2. **`addressed in commit`**:
   - The word `commit` is a prefix of `commitment`.
   - If a review summary says: *"This was addressed in commitment to our standards."*, it will match `addressed in commit` and be suppressed.
3. **`feedback was`**:
   - The word `was` is a prefix of `waste` or `wash`.
   - If a review says: *"This feedback waste of time should be ignored."*, it will match `feedback was` and be suppressed.

#### Solution:
Add word boundaries (`\b`) to the vulnerable keywords and phrases to ensure they only match complete words. Additionally, avoid using the word 'issue' (such as in `no issues to report`) in the filtering keywords to prevent false positives.

```suggestion
NOOP_RE="(I have no feedback to provide|no feedback to provide|have no feedback|have no suggestions|no actionable feedback|no actionable suggestions|no further feedback|no suggestions to (add\b|provide\b|make\b)|no review comments|feedback was\b (already\b )?(provided\b|addressed\b|corrected\b)|addressed in commit\b|already\b (fixed\b|resolved\b|addressed\b)|has been\b (resolved\b|addressed\b|fixed\b))"
```

If an active ruleset does not have any `ref_name` conditions (for example, if it targets all branches or is structured differently), `.conditions.ref_name` will be `null` or missing. In `jq`, attempting to index `null` with a string (like `.conditions.ref_name.include`) throws a fatal error, causing `jq` to exit with a non-zero status. This triggers the `|| return 1` fallback, causing the function to fail closed and block all merges. Using optional chaining (`?.`) in `jq` prevents this error and safely defaults to an empty array. 		exclude_patterns=$(printf '%s' "$detail" | jq -r '.conditions?.ref_name?.exclude // [] | .[]') || return 1

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similarly, if a rule of type `pull_request` does not contain a `.parameters` object, attempting to access `.parameters.required_approving_review_count` will throw a fatal `jq` error and fail closed. Using optional chaining (`?.`) ensures safe navigation. Also, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on commands that parse configuration files (like `jq`) so that actual syntax or system errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
		approval_count=$(printf '%s' "$detail" | jq -r '[.rules[]? | select(.type == "pull_request") | (.parameters?.required_approving_review_count // 0)] | max // 0') || {
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on commands that parse configuration files (e.g., `jq`), as it can hide syntax errors and make debugging difficult.
2. In `jq`, use the fallback operator `//` to provide a default value for expressions that might result in `null`, such as `min_by` or `max_by` on empty or invalid inputs.
</details>

Refactor `cmd_api_budget` to pre-compute the stats and log counts in a single pass before rendering. This avoids spawning `jq` 6 times and `grep` 4 times on the same files, significantly reducing process and I/O overhead.

```shell
cmd_api_budget() {
	local json_output=0
	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
		local opt="$1"
		case "$opt" in
			--json)
				json_output=1
				shift
				;;
			-h|--help)
				cmd_help
				return 0
				;;
			*)
				print_error "unknown api-budget option: $opt"
				cmd_help
				return 1
				;;
		esac
	done

	local stats_file="" logfile=""
	stats_file=$(_resolve_stats_file)
	logfile=$(_resolve_logfile "")

	local circuit="0" reserve="0" deferred="0" force_rest="0" cache_prime_runs="0" cache_prime_failures="0"
	if [[ -f "$stats_file" && -s "$stats_file" ]] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		read -r circuit reserve deferred force_rest cache_prime_runs cache_prime_failures < <(
			jq -r '[
				.pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken // 0,
				.pulse_graphql_budget_reserve_mode // 0,
				.pulse_graphql_budget_stage_deferred // 0,
				.pulse_graphql_budget_force_rest_reads // 0,
				.pulse_cache_prime_runs // 0,
				.pulse_cache_prime_failures // 0
			] | @tsv' "$stats_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0 0 0 0 0 0"
		)
	fi

	local pr_cache_hits="0" pr_cache_misses="0" rest_mentions="0" graphql_mentions="0"
	if [[ -f "$logfile" ]]; then
		read -r pr_cache_hits pr_cache_misses rest_mentions graphql_mentions < <(
			awk '
			BEGIN {
				pat1 = "gh_pr_view.*cache.*hit|cache.*hit.*gh_pr_view"
				pat2 = "gh_pr_view.*cache.*miss|cache.*miss.*gh_pr_view"
				pat3 = "rest fallback|force_rest|rest reads"
				pat4 = "graphql"
			}
			{
				lower = tolower($0)
				if (lower ~ pat1) c1++
				if (lower ~ pat2) c2++
				if (lower ~ pat3) c3++
				if (lower ~ pat4) c4++
			}
			END {
				print (c1 ? c1 : 0), (c2 ? c2 : 0), (c3 ? c3 : 0), (c4 ? c4 : 0)
			}' "$logfile" 2>/dev/null || echo "0 0 0 0"
		)
	fi

	if [[ "$json_output" -eq 1 ]]; then
		_api_budget_render_json "$stats_file" "$logfile" \
			"$circuit" "$reserve" "$deferred" "$force_rest" "$cache_prime_runs" "$cache_prime_failures" \
			"$pr_cache_hits" "$pr_cache_misses" "$rest_mentions" "$graphql_mentions"
		return 0
	fi
	_api_budget_render_text "$stats_file" "$logfile" \
		"$circuit" "$reserve" "$deferred" "$force_rest" "$cache_prime_runs" "$cache_prime_failures" \
		"$pr_cache_hits" "$pr_cache_misses" "$rest_mentions" "$graphql_mentions"
	return 0
}
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Writing the metadata file directly using redirection (`>`) is not atomic. If another concurrent process checks the lock's staleness after the file is created but before the shell finishes writing the `created_at` timestamp, it will read an empty or incomplete file. This causes `created_at` to default to `0`, leading the other process to falsely identify the lock as stale and delete it.

To prevent this race condition, write the metadata to a temporary file first and then atomically rename it using `mv`. Stream the multi-line content using a command group `{...}` for better readability and efficiency.

```suggestion
_prrts_write_lock_metadata() {
	local lock_dir="$1"
	local now_epoch="$2"
	{
		printf 'pid=%s\n' "$$"
		printf 'created_at=%s\n' "$now_epoch"
	} >"${lock_dir}/metadata.tmp"
	mv "${lock_dir}/metadata.tmp" "${lock_dir}/metadata"
	return 0
}
```

Reclaiming a stale lock by directly calling `_prrts_remove_lock_dir` followed by `mkdir` introduces a critical TOCTOU (time-of-check to time-of-use) race condition. If multiple concurrent processes simultaneously detect that the lock is stale, they will all attempt to remove the directory and recreate it. This can result in one process deleting a newly acquired, valid lock directory that was just created by another process.

To safely reclaim a stale lock, atomically rename the stale lock directory using `mv` first. Only the process that successfully renames the directory should proceed to delete it and acquire the new lock. Avoid using `2>/dev/null` to suppress errors on the `mv` operation, as the lock's existence has already been verified by the preceding staleness check.

```suggestion

			_prrts_remove_lock_dir "$stale_rename"
			if mkdir "$lock_dir"; then

				return 0
```

The current prefix-stripping logic only handles standard `https://`, `http://`, and `git@` prefixes. It fails to normalize other common git remote URL formats, such as `ssh://git@github.com/`, `git://github.com/`, or URLs containing credentials (e.g., `https://token@github.com/`). We can simplify and make this much more robust by using wildcard pattern stripping to remove everything up to `github.com/` or `github.com:`.

```
_shim_normalize_repo_slug() {
	local target="$1"
	target="${target#*github.com/}"
	target="${target#*github.com:}"
	target="${target%.git}"
	if [[ "$target" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]; then
		printf '%s\n' "$target"
		return 0
	fi
	return 1
}
```

While removing the wildcard fallback `*) [[ -z "$path" ]] && path="$arg" ;;` from `_shim_repo_from_api_path_args` successfully hardens path extraction for that function, the exact same pattern still exists in two other critical functions in this file:

1. `_shim_api_is_write_endpoint` (around line 605)
2. `_shim_api_target_from_path` (around line 633)

Because these functions still have the `*)` fallback, and common short flags like `-q` (for `--jq`) or `-t` (for `--template`) are not in their double-increment lists, any argument passed to those short flags (e.g., `-q .`) will be incorrectly captured as the API `path`.

This causes `_shim_api_is_write_endpoint` to fail to recognize write endpoints, which **completely bypasses the headless external write guard, signature injection, and privacy scan** when short flags are used.

### Recommendation
Remove the `*)` fallback case from both `_shim_api_is_write_endpoint` and `_shim_api_target_from_path` as well, since they also only care about paths starting with `/repos/` or `repos/`.

Using `\$` in a Basic Regular Expression (BRE) to match a literal `$` can lead to portability issues across different `grep` implementations (such as GNU grep vs. BSD grep on macOS). The current implementation of `_worker_db_migration_ledgers_match_shared` is highly vulnerable to transient SQLite errors (such as database locks or timeouts). If `sqlite3_with_timeout` fails on the shared database, the `|| printf '0'` fallback executes, resulting in `shared_count=0`. This causes `expected_ledgers` to remain `0`, which ultimately makes the function return `1` (mismatch). Consequently, `_sync_worker_db_migration_metadata` will destructively archive the active worker database via `_archive_partial_worker_db`, leading to accidental data loss or startup failures under concurrent load.

To prevent this, we should query `sqlite_master` first to check if the table exists, and explicitly check the exit status of the `sqlite3` command. If a transient error occurs (non-zero exit code), we should abort the check safely and return `0` (indicating a match/no-op) to avoid destructive archiving. Additionally, we avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` to ensure any system or syntax issues remain visible for debugging.

```shell
_worker_db_migration_ledgers_match_shared() {
	local worker_db="$1"
	local shared_db="$2"
	local ledger_table shared_count worker_count expected_ledgers=0
	local rc has_table

	[[ -f "$worker_db" && -f "$shared_db" ]] || return 1
	for ledger_table in __drizzle_migrations data_migration migration; do
		# Check if table exists in shared DB first to avoid errors and distinguish transient failures
		has_table=$(sqlite3_with_timeout "$shared_db" "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='${ledger_table}' LIMIT 1;")
		rc=$?
		if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
			# Transient error (e.g. database locked). Return 0 to avoid destructive archiving.
			return 0
		fi
		if [[ -z "$has_table" ]]; then
			continue
		fi

		shared_count=$(sqlite3_with_timeout "$shared_db" "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM main.\"${ledger_table}\";")
		rc=$?
		if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
			return 0
		fi
		[[ "$shared_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || shared_count=0
		if [[ "$shared_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
			continue
		fi
		expected_ledgers=1

		# Check if table exists in worker DB
		has_table=$(sqlite3_with_timeout "$worker_db" "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='${ledger_table}' LIMIT 1;")
		rc=$?
		if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
			return 0
		fi
		if [[ -z "$has_table" ]]; then
			return 1
		fi

		worker_count=$(sqlite3_with_timeout "$worker_db" "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM main.\"${ledger_table}\";")
		rc=$?
		if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
			return 0
		fi
		[[ "$worker_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || worker_count=0
		if [[ "$worker_count" -lt "$shared_count" ]]; then
			return 1
		fi
	done

	return 0
}
```

### High Severity Issue: Potential Data Loss / Migration Replay on Attachment Failure

If the `ATTACH DATABASE` command on line 1064 fails (for example, due to database locks, permission issues, or a missing shared database file), the execution will still proceed to the `DELETE` statement. This will completely empty the worker's migration ledger table (`${ledger_table}`).

Since the subsequent `INSERT` statement will also fail (as the `shared` database is not attached), the worker DB will be left with a completely empty migration ledger. This will cause OpenCode/Drizzle to treat the schema as unmigrated, replaying all migrations and failing with "table already exists" errors.

#### Recommended Solution
To make this operation atomic and safe, wrap the `DELETE` and `INSERT` statements in a transaction and enable `.bail on` so that any failure during attachment or insertion aborts the execution and rolls back the deletion. Avoid blanket suppression of errors on the command call to ensure any syntax or system issues remain visible for debugging:

```bash
sqlite3_with_timeout "$worker_db" <<-SQL
	.bail on
	ATTACH DATABASE '${shared_db_sql}' AS shared;
	BEGIN TRANSACTION;
	DELETE FROM main."${ledger_table}";
	INSERT INTO main."${ledger_table}" SELECT * FROM shared."${ledger_table}";
	COMMIT;
	DETACH DATABASE shared;
SQL
```

This ensures that if `ATTACH` or `INSERT` fails, the transaction is rolled back, leaving the existing ledger rows intact.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

Using `HEAD` to count commits on the orphan branch is incorrect here. Because the worktree is always reset to `origin/main` (or the base branch) in `_dlw_precreate_worktree` before this check is run, `HEAD` will always point to the base branch, resulting in a commit count of `0`. This causes the `zero_commits` check to falsely trigger and block dispatches on reused worktrees. We should check `origin/${branch_name}` instead of `HEAD` to accurately count the commits on the remote orphan branch. Additionally, avoid using `2>/dev/null` to suppress stderr so that any git errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
		commit_count=$(git -C "$worktree_path" rev-list --count "origin/${base_branch}..origin/${branch_name}" || true)
		if ! [[ "$commit_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
			commit_count=$(git -C "$worktree_path" rev-list --count "origin/${branch_name}" || true)
		fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid using '2>/dev/null' for blanket suppression of command errors in shell scripts to ensure that authentication, syntax, or system issues remain visible for debugging.
</details>

Running `git ls-remote` without disabling terminal prompts can cause the background pulse dispatch loop to hang indefinitely if the remote repository requires authentication or if credentials are not configured. Prefixing the command with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` ensures that Git fails fast instead of waiting for interactive input. Additionally, avoid using `2>&1` to suppress stderr so that authentication or network errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
		if [[ -n "$worktree_path" && ( -d "$worktree_path/.git" || -f "$worktree_path/.git" ) ]]; then
			GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -C "$worktree_path" ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/heads/${branch_name}" >/dev/null || remote_rc=$?
		else
			GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/heads/${branch_name}" >/dev/null || remote_rc=$?
		fi
```

In the current architecture of `pulse-merge-feedback.sh`, `_emit_ci_failure_guidance_blocks` groups failures by classification and performs a lookup in the configuration file, breaking on the first match of the classification name (e.g., `TIMEOUT_NO_OUTPUT`).

As a result, only the guidance text of the first matching classification entry (`*[Tt]imeout*`) will ever be emitted. The specific guidance texts for `*[Ww]atchdog*` and `*[Rr]unner*communication*` are unreachable dead code.

Consider consolidating these patterns under a single `TIMEOUT_NO_OUTPUT` entry with a generalized guidance text, or refactoring the emitter to support pattern-specific guidance lookup.

The current lock acquisition implementation in `_gh_secondary_read_ramp_take_token` immediately returns `0` (success/allow) if the lock directory cannot be created. Under high concurrency (e.g., multiple parallel read/prefetch operations), lock contention will cause `mkdir` to fail, allowing all concurrent requests to bypass the ramp budget entirely. Additionally, if a process is interrupted or crashes while holding the lock, the lock directory becomes stale, permanently disabling the read ramp pacing.

To resolve this, implement a robust lock acquisition mechanism with a retry loop, a small backoff/sleep, and stale lock detection (by checking if the process that created the lock is still running). Also, use `rm -rf` instead of `rmdir` to clean up the lock directory since it will contain a `pid` file. Simplify the stale lock cleanup by checking the dependent pid file directly rather than adding redundant pre-checks on the lock directory.

```shell
	local attempt=0
	while ! mkdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null; do
		local lock_pid
		lock_pid=$(cat "$lock_dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
		if [[ -n "$lock_pid" ]] && ! kill -0 "$lock_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
			rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
			continue
		fi
		attempt=$((attempt + 1))
		if [[ "$attempt" -ge 5 ]]; then
			return 1
		fi
		sleep 0.1
	done
	echo "$$" > "$lock_dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true

	if [[ -r "$file" ]]; then
		IFS=$'\t' read -r old_phase old_minute old_count <"$file" || true
	fi
	if [[ "$old_phase" == "$phase" && "$old_minute" == "$minute" && "$old_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
		count="$old_count"
	fi
	if [[ "$count" -ge "$AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_RAMP_BUDGET" ]]; then
		rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
		return 1
	fi
	count=$((count + 1))
	printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$phase" "$minute" "$count" >"${file}.tmp" 2>/dev/null || {
		rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
		return 0
	}
	mv "${file}.tmp" "$file" 2>/dev/null || true
	rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
	return 0
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

There are two potential issues in this `jq` filter:

1. **Null Pointer / Indexing Error**: If a user account has been deleted, the GitHub API returns `.user` as `null`. Attempting to access `.user.login` directly will throw a `Cannot index null with string "login"` error in `jq`, causing the entire command to fail and return an exit code of 5. This will make the helper function fail and return `1`. Using error suppression (`.user.login?` and `.author.login?`) prevents this crash.
2. **Regex Simplification**: Instead of using a regex `test` with start-of-line anchors, we can use the simpler and more efficient `startswith` builtin function, which is cleaner and less prone to regex engine quirks.

```suggestion
		| [ .[] | select(
			((.author_association // "NONE") as $a | ($a != "OWNER" and $a != "MEMBER"))
			and (((.user.login? // .author.login? // "") as $login
				| ((($login == "github-actions[bot]") or ($login == "github-actions"))
					and ((.body // "") | (startswith("<!-- nmr-hold-guidance -->") or startswith("<!-- ever-nmr-remediation -->"))))) | not)
		) ]
```

In `_gh_secondary_cooldown_trim_events`, if the file size exceeds `max_bytes` but the line count is already at or below `max_lines`, calling `tail -n "$max_lines"` will not reduce the file size at all. This results in an ineffective byte-limit check and a redundant write operation. To guarantee that the file size is actually reduced when it exceeds `max_bytes`, consider tailing a smaller fraction of lines (e.g., half of `max_lines`). Additionally, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on the file operation to ensure any issues (like permission errors) are visible.

```suggestion
	if [[ "$byte_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$byte_count" -gt "$max_bytes" ]]; then
		tmp="${file}.tmp"
		local half_lines=$((max_lines / 2))
		[[ "$half_lines" -gt 0 ]] || half_lines=1
		tail -n "$half_lines" "$file" >"$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$file" || rm -f "$tmp"
	fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid using 2>/dev/null to suppress errors on file operations if the file's existence has already been verified by a preceding check. This practice is redundant for 'file not found' errors and can mask other important issues like permissions problems.
</details>

![security-medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-medium-priority.svg) ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

While using `HOME` as a fallback is much more secure than `/tmp`, the fallback path is currently not pre-created with secure permissions. This means the file created by shell redirection (`2>`) will use the default umask, potentially making the captured stderr world-readable if the user's home directory is accessible by other local users.

Additionally, if `HOME` has a trailing slash (or is `/`), the path could result in a double slash (e.g., `//.aidevops...`), which has special meaning on some POSIX-compliant systems (like Cygwin/MSYS2).

We can improve both security and robustness by:
1. Stripping any trailing slash from `HOME` using `${HOME%/}`.
2. Pre-creating the file with `touch` and restricting its permissions to `0600` using `chmod`, matching the secure behavior of `mktemp`.

Note: Avoid using `2>/dev/null` on the `chmod` command since the file's existence is already verified by the preceding `touch` check, ensuring any permission issues are not silently masked.

```suggestion
_claim_post_error_fallback_path() {
	if [[ -n "${HOME:-}" && -d "$HOME" && -w "$HOME" ]]; then
		local path="${HOME%/}/.aidevops-claim-post-error.$$.$RANDOM"
		if touch "$path" 2>/dev/null; then
			chmod 600 "$path" || true
			printf '%s' "$path"
			return 0
		fi
	fi

	printf '%s\n' "Error: mktemp failed and HOME is unavailable for secure claim POST stderr capture" >&2
	return 1
}
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

When `check_dispatch_dedup` blocks, it can be due to various reasons checked inside `is_assigned` (such as `no-auto-dispatch`, `infrastructure`, `hold-for-review`, `dispatch cooldown`, or `cost budget`). Currently, any block from `check_dispatch_dedup` is unconditionally logged as `reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked` in `$LOGFILE`. This shadows the actual block reason and causes incorrect classification in metrics.

We can capture the stdout of `check_dispatch_dedup` to extract the actual block signal and log a precise `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON` with the correct `reason` and `signal` fields, while keeping the default fallback to ensure existing tests pass.

```shell
	local _dedup_out=""
	_dedup_out=$(ISSUE_META_JSON="$issue_meta_json" \
		check_dispatch_dedup "$issue_number" "$repo_slug" "$dispatch_title" "$issue_title" "$self_login") || _dedup_rc=$?
	if [[ "$_dedup_rc" -eq 0 || "$_dedup_rc" -eq 3 ]]; then
		if [[ -n "$_dedup_out" ]]; then
			printf '%s\n' "$_dedup_out"
		fi
		local _sig
		_sig=$(printf '%s' "$_dedup_out" | head -n 1)
		_sig="${_sig:-dedup_guard_blocked}"
		local _reason="dedup_active_claim"
		local _lower_sig
		_lower_sig=$(printf '%s' "$_sig" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
		if [[ "$_lower_sig" == *"no-auto-dispatch"* || "$_lower_sig" == *"infrastructure"* || "$_lower_sig" == *"hold-for-review"* || "$_lower_sig" == *"parent-task"* ]]; then
			_reason="policy_gate"
		elif [[ "$_lower_sig" == *"cooldown"* ]]; then
			_reason="cooldown_no_worker_process"
		elif [[ "$_lower_sig" == *"budget"* ]]; then
			_reason="cost_budget_exceeded"
		fi
		if [[ "$_reason" == "dedup_active_claim" && "$_sig" == "dedup_guard_blocked" ]]; then
			echo "[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked issue=#${issue_number} repo=${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"
		else
			echo "[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=${_reason} signal=${_sig} issue=#${issue_number} repo=${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"
		fi
		echo "[dispatch_with_dedup] Dedup guard blocked #${issue_number} in ${repo_slug}" >>"$LOGFILE"
```
